module_microarchitecture.name: request_orchestrator
module_microarchitecture.implementation_style: Synchronous ready/valid ingress wrapper with bounded-width request packing and transaction tracking.
module_microarchitecture.control_strategy: Capture geometry and flow descriptors only when both inputs are valid and the runtime side is ready; increment request_id monotonically on each accepted transaction; attach timestamp/cycle-age metadata; assert timeout deterministically when the watchdog threshold is exceeded.
module_microarchitecture.state_strategy: Use small synchronous registers for outstanding transaction status, request_id, timestamp, and configuration-readiness gating; clear all state on reset.
module_microarchitecture.output_strategy: Drive model request fields directly from registered packed descriptors and expose request/timeout status without any physics interpretation.
ownership_notes: Owns request_id generation and outstanding-transaction bookkeeping.
Owns the packed request payload fields it emits.
Does not perform inference or alter model semantics beyond packing and sequencing.

module_microarchitecture.name: domino_runtime_interface
module_microarchitecture.implementation_style: Protocol adapter and response qualifier for the external NVIDIA DoMINO runtime.
module_microarchitecture.control_strategy: Compare response request_id against the outstanding request_id, check freshness and ordering against the programmable threshold, and only qualify a response when both integrity and sequencing checks pass.
module_microarchitecture.state_strategy: Maintain minimal synchronous correlation state and comparison qualifiers; no complex FSM is implied beyond handshake and qualification bookkeeping.
module_microarchitecture.output_strategy: Forward qualified response payloads only after ID and freshness checks succeed; otherwise assert stale/mismatch fault indication and suppress response qualification.
ownership_notes: Owns response_match and freshness_ok qualification logic.
Owns the validated response payloads released downstream.
Does not synthesize actuator behavior or perform local surrogate inference.

module_microarchitecture.name: command_synthesis_engine
module_microarchitecture.implementation_style: Deterministic fixed-point arithmetic block or simple ROM/table-assisted mapping stage.
module_microarchitecture.control_strategy: When a qualified response is present, combine drag/lift/pressure/meta inputs with configuration gains and bias to produce a raw actuator command candidate; otherwise hold raw output invalid.
module_microarchitecture.state_strategy: Prefer purely combinational math with optional registered output staging for timing closure; no dynamic control flow is required.
module_microarchitecture.output_strategy: Emit only a raw command candidate and validity qualifier for downstream clamping; never drive actuator outputs directly.
ownership_notes: Owns the raw command candidate before clamping.
Does not own any final actuator output interface.
Must not expose unclamped values at the top level.

module_microarchitecture.name: actuator_clamper
module_microarchitecture.implementation_style: Saturating limiter with deterministic min/max enforcement on the actuator command bus.
module_microarchitecture.control_strategy: Clamp every valid raw command to cfg_actuator_min/cfg_actuator_max and raise clamp_event whenever saturation occurs.
module_microarchitecture.state_strategy: Minimal synchronous register or purely combinational comparison/saturation path is sufficient; any event reporting should be registered for clean telemetry if needed.
module_microarchitecture.output_strategy: Provide only clamped command data and its valid qualifier; unclamped values remain internal and are never exposed externally.
ownership_notes: Owns the clamped command representation passed to arbitration.
Owns clamp_event visibility for telemetry and fault handling.
No unbounded or non-deterministic behavior is introduced.

module_microarchitecture.name: safe_fallback_manager
module_microarchitecture.implementation_style: Deterministic safe-state generator with a simple synchronous mode-hold behavior.
module_microarchitecture.control_strategy: Assert fallback whenever reset, configuration-not-ready, timeout, stale/mismatch, payload corruption, model unavailability, invalid input, or internal fault is present; otherwise release the safe output only when health and configuration conditions permit.
module_microarchitecture.state_strategy: Use a small synchronous mode/state register to hold fallback active until the required clear/readiness conditions are satisfied.
module_microarchitecture.output_strategy: Drive a predefined safe actuator command through the same top-level clamping/arbitration path as the model-derived command.
ownership_notes: Owns the safe fallback command source.
Does not bypass clamping or arbitration.

module_microarchitecture.name: safety_supervisor
module_microarchitecture.implementation_style: Final arbitration and sticky-fault aggregation stage.
module_microarchitecture.control_strategy: Prioritize fallback command source over model-derived command whenever any fault, mismatch, stale condition, timeout, or configuration-not-ready condition is asserted; otherwise select the clamped model-derived command.
module_microarchitecture.state_strategy: Retain sticky fault status in synchronous registers until the defined clear mechanism is applied; use minimal state sufficient to remember fault-latched conditions and selected source.
module_microarchitecture.output_strategy: Emit the final actuator_cmd_valid, actuator_cmd, fault_valid, fault_code, and source_select outputs with no direct model-to-actuator bypass path.
ownership_notes: Owns final output arbitration and source selection.
Prevents any direct model-to-actuator bypass path.

fsm_intent.name: request_orchestrator
fsm_intent.description: A small synchronous transaction-control FSM is implied to manage idle, request-accepted, awaiting-response, and timeout conditions, but it should remain minimal and directly tied to ready/valid handshake and watchdog bookkeeping.

fsm_intent.name: domino_runtime_interface
fsm_intent.description: A minimal synchronous qualifier FSM is implied to manage unmatched, matched, and stale/mismatch response handling around the external runtime handshake.

fsm_intent.name: command_synthesis_engine
fsm_intent.description: No explicit FSM is required; combinational or single-stage pipelined arithmetic is sufficient.

fsm_intent.name: actuator_clamper
fsm_intent.description: No explicit FSM is required; saturating compare-and-select logic is sufficient.

fsm_intent.name: safe_fallback_manager
fsm_intent.description: A small deterministic mode-hold FSM is implied to ensure safe outputs on reset and to remain in fallback until configuration and health conditions are satisfied.

fsm_intent.name: safety_supervisor
fsm_intent.description: A minimal arbitration/fault-latch FSM or synchronous decision logic is implied to select model versus fallback source and preserve sticky fault behavior.

output_mapping: model_req_valid driven from accepted transaction state
model_req_id driven from request_id counter
model_req_timestamp driven from timestamp/cycle-age counter
model_req_geometry driven from packed geometry descriptor
model_req_stream_velocity_mps driven from packed flow descriptor field
model_req_geometry_tag driven from configuration provenance tag
timeout_event driven from watchdog compare
vehicle_geometry_ready and flow_conditions_ready driven by acceptance/backpressure policy
model_req_ready and model_resp_ready expressed as protocol readiness toward the external runtime and request path
response_match asserted only when response id equals outstanding id
freshness_ok asserted only when timing/order checks pass
response_valid_qualified gates all downstream response payloads
qualified response outputs reflect only accepted payloads
stale_or_mismatch_fault asserted on stale, duplicated, mismatched, or corrupted responses

internal_storage: optional pipeline register for raw command
optional ROM/table lookup values if used
output_mapping: raw_actuator_cmd computed deterministically from qualified response fields and configuration gains/bias
raw_cmd_valid asserted only when response_valid_qualified is true
clamped_actuator_cmd equals raw command when in range, otherwise nearest legal bound
clamped_cmd_valid follows raw_cmd_valid through the limiter stage
clamp_event asserts when saturation occurs
fallback_cmd driven from cfg_safe_actuator_cmd or registered safe constant
fallback_cmd_valid asserted when fallback command is actively selected
fallback_active asserted whenever fallback mode is required
actuator_cmd_valid and actuator_cmd selected from either clamped model-derived path or fallback path
source_select indicates origin of final command
fault_valid reflects sticky or current fault conditions
fault_code encodes stale/mismatch, timeout, invalid input, payload corruption, model unavailable, or configuration-not-ready conditions

sequencing_notes: All state transitions are synchronous to clk and reset behavior is active-low through rst_n.
The request path should accept geometry and flow descriptors only when the respective ready/valid handshakes permit it and configuration is complete.
A new request_id is issued monotonically for every accepted model transaction.
The response path should accept only the response matching the outstanding request_id and only if freshness/ordering checks pass.
Valid response payloads must be qualified before entering command synthesis; no direct response-to-actuator connection is allowed.

Fallback and supervisory arbitration must always override model-derived command selection on reset, timeout, mismatch, stale response, invalid input, payload corruption, model unavailability, or internal fault.
Sticky faults remain asserted until the defined clear mechanism is applied.
timing_notes: The design should be synthesizable with simple flip-flops, combinational logic, counters, comparators, saturating arithmetic, and optional small ROMs only.
No numeric performance guarantee is implied beyond the configured watchdog and freshness thresholds.
A bounded-latency request-to-response flow is supported by handshake, but the implementation should not assume a fixed external runtime latency.
If pipelining is needed for timing closure, keep it shallow and deterministic; avoid introducing unnecessary FSM complexity.
The unclamped command path must remain internal and never appear at the top-level outputs.
consistency_notes: No hierarchy, ports, or filenames may differ from digital_spec_json.
